Subject: Horizon BI — Legal questionnaire and order form clarifications

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're wrapping the RFP and have a handful of follow-ups on the legal questionnaire and the attached order form. Two priority items for legal:

1) Liability cap scenarios — we need confirmation how Redwood treats catastrophic data exposure (PII) vs non-PII model-output regressions.
2) IP assignment/derivative rights for embeddings and outputs produced from our proprietary datasets.

I've attached the Horizon legal worksheet and the order form with redline comments on pages 2 and 4. Can you confirm who will own the official responses? We need the final answers and an updated order form by Friday, 26 Mar EOD PT to keep the procurement timeline.

Attachments: Horizon_Legal_Worksheet.xlsx (xlsx), Horizon_OrderForm_v4.docx (docx)

Subject: Re: Horizon BI — Legal questionnaire and order form clarifications

Elena / Aditya / Marissa —

Attached are Redwood's formal responses to the Horizon legal worksheet (see PDF). Below are the high-level positions and a short rationale for each of the primary asks you flagged:

1) Liability cap
- Base position: liability cap tied to net fees paid in the prior 12 months (standard multiple).
- Catastrophic PII exposure: we acknowledge the sensitivity. For confirmed PII exposure resulting from our systems, Redwood will agree to an elevated cap: carve-out to increase to $5,000,000 limited to direct damages arising from security failures where Redwood is adjudicated liable. We will not accept open-ended punitive/indirect claims.

2) IP / outputs
- Customer retains ownership of Customer Data (including proprietary datasets uploaded by Horizon).
- Outputs generated by the model are governed by the order form license: Horizon gets a worldwide, perpetual, royalty-free license to use outputs for internal business purposes. Redwood does not claim ownership of customer data or customer-derived embeddings.

3) Indemnity
- Redwood accepts indemnity for willful misconduct and breaches of Redwood's obligations (data security, confidentiality). We will not accept indemnity for third-party claims based solely on customer's use of outputs (i.e., downstream user misuse). We propose mutual indemnities with limited scope and step-in remedies.

4) Insurance
- Standard requirement: Commercial general liability + Technology E&O; minimum combined limits of $3M per occurrence / $5M aggregate. For the elevated liability carve-out (PII), we request confirmation Horizon's carrier or self-insured retention details for contract clarity.

5) Order form exhibits
- We propose two clean exhibits: (a) SOW describing data segregation and retention, (b) Security exhibit listing logging/audit retention and KMS options. These are attached as exhibit drafts.

I've included short, negotiation-friendly redlines in the attached PDF. If Horizon needs the $5M cap to be unconditional, we'll need to circle back to commercial to confirm rate/commitment adjustments.

Attachments: Redwood_Legal_Final_Responses.pdf (pdf), Exhibit_SOW_DataSegregation.docx (docx)

Regards,
Laura Bennett

Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 11:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Horizon BI — Legal questionnaire and order form clarifications

Laura — thanks for the quick and detailed response. A few follow-ups from our counsel after reviewing your PDF:

• The proposed $5M carve-out for confirmed PII exposure is a good starting point. Our counsel wants language clarifying the trigger ("confirmed exposure caused by Redwood's systems") and a short list of examples. Can you add brief objective triggers to avoid long disputes?

• Insurance: Horizon requires the vendor to carry at least $5M in Tech E&O for enterprise agreements of our size (we commit to a 3-year term). Please confirm Redwood can meet $5M limits or provide evidence of an alternative arrangement (higher retention + excess carriers).

• Order form redlines: we attached the marked-up order form (Horizon_OrderForm_v4_redlines.docx). The main commercial ask is to include a 4-hour support response SLA for severity 1 incidents during business hours and a limited credit schedule.

We appreciate the willingness to be flexible on IP ownership for outputs. For the embedding rights, our engineer side requests explicit confirmation that embeddings derived from our data can be exported and retained by Horizon in perpetuity.

Attachments: Horizon_OrderForm_v4_redlines.docx (docx)

Best,
Elena

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: internal: commercial approach on Horizon liability request

Aditya / Marissa — quick internal note before I respond to Elena:

Proposed commercial levers:
- Accept $5M carve-out for PII exposure limited to direct damages; require Horizon to provide SOC2 + recent pentest and confirm environment scope (prod only).
- Increase Tech E&O minimum to $5M but request higher subscription commitment (24–36 months) or a modest price uplift (~8–12%).
- Add a 4-hour P1 response SLA during business hours with a capped credit schedule (max 2 weeks of credits per year).

If you agree I will draft a short commercial note tying the elevated liability to the 3-year commitment and draft the necessary pricing language. Need buy-in from Marissa on discount/commit adjustments.

—Rohan

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Vos <elena.vos@horizonbi.com>, Samir Khan <samir.k@horizonbi.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Horizon BI — Legal questionnaire and order form clarifications

Elena / Samir — thanks for the review and the redlines. To summarize and confirm next steps so procurement can close the loop:

1) Liability cap: Redwood will accept a $5,000,000 liability cap specific to confirmed PII exposures caused by Redwood's systems, limited to direct damages. We'll add objective trigger language: confirmed by mutual forensic report and root-cause analysis attributing the exposure to Redwood.

2) Insurance: Redwood can amend our insurance requirement to Tech E&O at $5M per occurrence (we will provide certificate of insurance and summary of coverage).

3) SLA: We will include a 4-hour business-hours response for P1 incidents and a capped service credit schedule (draft language attached).

4) Embeddings/IP: Redwood confirms Horizon may export and retain embeddings derived from Horizon's data in perpetuity for internal business purposes; we'll add a clause clarifying use restrictions (no resale of embeddings).

5) Commercial trade: To offer the elevated cap and higher insurance, we request a 36-month commitment at the contracted usage tier; Rohan has proposed a modest price adjustment which we will call out in the revised order form.

I've attached: Redwood_Revised_OrderForm_HZN_v2.docx with the legal and commercial redlines, plus a DocuSign link to execute once you confirm acceptance of the above points.

Attachments: Redwood_Revised_OrderForm_HZN_v2.docx (docx)
Link: https://www.docusign.net/sign/Redwood-HZN-OrderForm

If that matches Horizon's expectations we can move to signature and target a go-live the week after signing.
